relationship.statement: A pendulum's period depends only on its string length and gravity, not on the bob's mass. Longer strings slow the swing down, stronger gravity speeds it up, and at small angles the release angle sets the swing width without changing the period.
assumptions: The string is massless and rigid, with the bob treated as a point mass.
Air resistance and pivot friction are zero, so the swing keeps constant energy.
The period formula uses the small-angle approximation for swings near vertical.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot point to the center of the bob

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration pulling the bob toward vertical

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the hanging bob, which cancels out of swing timing

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Initial angle pulled away from the vertical resting line

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time taken to complete one full back-and-forth swing

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete back-and-forth swings per second

quantities.label: Current angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angle from vertical as the pendulum swings

quantities.label: Max speed
quantities.meaning: Peak speed of the bob at the lowest point of its arc

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = 1.5; var theta0 = 25; var theta0Rad = theta0 * Math.PI / 180; var g = inputs.gravity; var gRef = 9.8; var period = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); var frequency = 1 / period; var omega = 2 * Math.PI / period; var angle = theta0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var angleRad = angle * Math.PI / 180; var bob_x = -0.7 + L * Math.sin(angleRad); var bob_y = 1.5 - L * Math.cos(angleRad); var grav_start_y = bob_y - 0.16; var grav_tip_y = grav_start_y - 0.035 * g; var max_speed = Math.sqrt(2 * g * L * (1 - Math.cos(theta0Rad))); var refPeriod = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / gRef); var refOmega = 2 * Math.PI / refPeriod; var ref_angle = theta0 * Math.cos(refOmega * t); var refAngleRad = ref_angle * Math.PI / 180; var ref_x = 0.7 + L * Math.sin(refAngleRad); var ref_y = 1.5 - L * Math.cos(refAngleRad); var ref_grav_start_y = ref_y - 0.16; var ref_grav_tip_y = ref_grav_start_y - 0.035 * gRef; var is_slower = g < gRef - 0.05; var is_faster = g > gRef + 0.05; return { period: period, frequency: frequency, angle: angle, max_speed: max_speed, bob_x: bob_x, bob_y: bob_y, grav_start_y: grav_start_y, grav_tip_y: grav_tip_y, ref_angle: ref_angle, ref_x: ref_x, ref_y: ref_y, ref_grav_start_y: ref_grav_start_y, ref_grav_tip_y: ref_grav_tip_y, is_slower: is_slower, is_faster: is_faster }; }

always: Fixed: L = 1.5 m, m = 1 kg, 25 deg.
Higher g cuts period, boosts speed.

lesson.title: How Gravity Changes a Pendulum Swing
lesson.description: Compare an adjustable pendulum against an Earth reference with fixed length, mass, and release angle. Adjust gravity to see how swing timing and speed change.
lesson.instructions: Slide Gravity from 1.5 to 25.0 m/s² while both pendulums keep a 1.5 m string, 1 kg bob, and 25 deg release angle. Watch the arcs, arrows, live values, and angle-versus-time plot, or set 9.8 m/s² to match Earth.
lesson.goal: Stronger gravity shortens the period and raises frequency and max speed, while the release angle keeps the swing width unchanged.
